name: Malaria Consortium, digital net campaigns in South Sudan (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The model's name: Malaria Consortium, digital net campaigns in South Sudan (The Life You Can Save, 2025).

missing_data.note: Measured: the campaign's own household registration counted the people reached and the 13.55% more people found than projected, and the effect of nets on malaria and children's deaths is from the Cochrane review of randomised trials.

summary: Malaria Consortium supported South Sudan's health ministry in moving its mass bednet campaigns from paper to phones, registering and geo-tagging households. The Life You Can Save credits it with the 13.55% more people the digital registration found than the projections, counts the cost of their nets as well as Malaria Consortium's own, and estimates $98 per DALY averted. Our view values each child's death averted by age the site's way and discounts the net's later years; the biggest uncertainty is whether the extra people found would otherwise have gone without nets.

rows.label: Cost the sheet counts per dollar of Malaria Consortium's own (the nets leave the cost)
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The campaign's funders and the health ministry, who bought and handed out the nets for the extra people, carry out the work only because of the charity, so they are credited through the share below (mobiliser_share), not by counting their money in the cost (docs/normalization.md 2.24): counted in both, they would be cut twice. The evaluator view keeps The Life You Can Save's cost (1).

rows.label: The extra nets, at what their money would otherwise have done, as a share of the good done
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The cost of the nets for the extra people, valued at GiveWell's figure for what a dollar of Global Fund or President's Malaria Initiative money would otherwise have done (@givewell_shared.cf_value_global_fund, about 4.6 times cash; the site's figure for malaria funders' money, docs/normalization.md 2.20), over our healthy years gained. South Sudan's mass campaigns are paid for mostly by the Global Fund; the sheet doesn't say who paid for these nets. A cost of the resources Malaria Consortium mobilises: netted from the good before the mobiliser's share. The evaluator view counts the nets in the cost instead (0 here).

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): the charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work.

rows.label: Healthy years gained per dollar
rows.formula: (1 / cost_per_daly * ours_vs_tlycs * counterfactual_share * donor_cost_share) * adopter_cost_out * (1 - nets_cost_share_of_good) * mobiliser_share
rows.explainer:
The Life You Can Save's DALYs per dollar of all costs, with deaths valued by age, times the share due to Malaria Consortium, per dollar of Malaria Consortium's own cost (adopter_cost_out), net of what the nets' money would otherwise have done, times the charity's share of the good that others carry out (mobiliser_share).

With credit by share of resources on, times the share of Malaria Consortium's full cost paid in cash.
